Subject: Billing aggregation question for long-context commerce assistant

Hi Vanessa / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the assistant looks like a good fit for our storefront chat flows. Before we move to pilot procurement, finance asked for clarity on how you will bill our usage given our expected pattern: a single user conversation that keeps a ~40k-token long product/context window cached on our side (and in your KV cache) but will periodically do many short calls (search, price-check, upsell prompts) across that same session.

Specific asks:
- Do micro-requests inside the same session aggregate into a single context-length charge, or are we charged per-call tokens each time?
- How do you round when requests are short (e.g., 18 tokens)? Is there a minimum per-call floor?
- If we stream lots of tiny requests in bursts (5–10 calls/sec) but reuse the same prefix/kv, do we still hit session minimums?

We attached a very small sample of our projected activity and a few example call traces (acme_billing_sample.csv). Can you confirm what the invoice would look like for December and what options there are for smoothing/discounts for a pilot?

Thanks — Emma

Hi Emma — great questions, thanks for the sample file. I pulled the product and billing folks into this thread so we can be explicit. TL;DR: the platform is able to avoid double-charging for context reuse in most cases, and we can offer a pilot concession to smooth your first invoices. Details below.

How billing currently works (short form):
- Token accounting: each request is metered for input + output tokens.
- Context reuse / KV cache: when the same prefix or cached KV is reused across calls from the same session, we do not re-charge the full context tokens for every call — we only meter incremental tokens for the new prompt and the generated tokens.
- Aggregation window: by default we have a 30-minute conversation aggregation window for session-level context crediting (this groups calls that are part of the same conversation so you don’t pay full context repeatedly). If your calls are continuous beyond 30 minutes, you can opt into a longer aggregation (configurable up to 24 hours) at commit.
- Minimums & rounding: per-call rounding is to the nearest billing quantum (100 token quantum for your proposed model). We also have a per-call floor of 50 tokens for streaming microcalls for non-committed accounts; committed pilots can waive/adjust that floor.

Implications for Acme’s pattern:
- If you keep the single 40k context pinned in KV and calls reuse that prefix, you will not be billed 40k tokens on each micro-request — only the incremental tokens + a small per-call floor (unless you choose commit-based custom handling).
- For bursts of tiny calls: if calls are <50 tokens and you don’t commit, we round up to the 50-token floor. If we run under a dedicated pilot with a short-term commit, we can reduce the floor to 10 tokens and apply smoothing.

Pilot concession we propose:
- 3-month pilot: 20% off per-token list rates for generation + reduced per-call floor of 10 tokens applied to microcalls.
- Extended aggregation window: set to 12 hours for the pilot so your periodic heartbeats stay in-session.
- Invoice smoothing: we will apply a 30% smoothing credit for the first invoice to offset on-boarding spikes (applied as a line-item credit).

I attached a one-pager that summarizes the proposed concession (pilot_concession_onepager.pdf) and a simple sample invoice based on your CSV. If this looks good we can surface to finance and legal; I’ve included a HubSpot link and a DocuSign placeholder below.

Next step: are you free Wed 10–11am PT for a quick walkthrough of the sample invoice and to lock down the pilot window?
